title: Republican Bill Cassidy blames administration vaccine policy for measles deaths
description_short: Republican Bill Cassidy blames administration vaccine policy for measles deaths
description_medium: At a September 16, 2026 Senate hearing, Republican Senator Bill Cassidy linked recent measles deaths to administration vaccine policy and questioned surgeon-general nominee Nicole Saphier about vaccines and autism. Saphier said she did not believe childhood vaccines cause autism. The deaths and policies Cassidy cited are not identified in the event record.
description_long: At a Senate hearing on September 16, 2026, Republican Senator Bill Cassidy challenged the administration’s vaccine policy and messaging in connection with recent measles deaths. He also questioned surgeon-general nominee Nicole Saphier about claims linking childhood vaccines with autism. Saphier said she did not believe childhood vaccines cause autism. The exchange placed vaccine policy and the nominee’s public position under scrutiny during her confirmation process. Cassidy connected the deaths to administration decisions, but the record does not identify which deaths he cited or which policies he blamed. Those details are necessary to assess his claim and understand the evidence he presented. A transcript or reliable account of the hearing would establish the full exchange and the sources behind the death figures. Until then, the event can be described as a dispute over vaccine messaging during a confirmation hearing, but the factual basis for linking policy to specific measles deaths remains unclear.
